passage: In the office lounge on Monday, Zubin laid out his papers for the Thursday train to Jaipur. His colleague Chetan looked in. "Two of everything?" "Ticket in my email and a printout. ID photo in my phone and a copy in my bag. My sister's number on paper and in the phone." He had also noted the next two trains in case his was cancelled. On Thursday he reached the station early. The train was three hours late. He calmly checked the list, went to the counter, and rebooked on the next train. Chetan messaged, "How are you not panicking?" Zubin replied, "I did my panic on Monday."

qa.q: What did Zubin put in his bag as a second copy of his ID?
qa.a: Zubin put a copy of the ID photo in his bag.

qa.q: What was Zubin feeling when the train ran three hours late, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Zubin stayed calm, since he checked the list, went to the counter and rebooked, and joked that the panic had been done on Monday.

qa.q: What made the late train an inconvenience for Zubin instead of a disaster?
qa.a: Zubin had two copies of his papers, his sister's number in two places, an early arrival and a list of the next trains.

qa.q: What might Zubin's reply "I did my panic on Monday" mean to Chetan?
qa.a: Chetan may take it as a joke that carries a truth: the worry was spent on preparing earlier, so there was less to feel in the moment.

grounding: Shows a prepared traveller keeping tickets, ID and contacts in two places, arriving early and having a plan if a train is missed.

passage:
Dear Pooja,
You asked how I stayed calm when my flight was cancelled. Honestly, I did it on autopilot, because I had done the boring things first. My ticket was in my email and on paper. I kept two copies of my ID, one in my bag and one in a cloud folder. My sister's number was written in my notebook as well as my phone. I reached the airport early, so when the screen said cancelled, the desk was not yet crowded. I stood in line, showed my papers and was booked on the evening flight. It cost me half a day, not a whole trip. Here is my little checklist for you to copy. Dilnaz

qa.q: Where did Dilnaz keep the two copies of the ID?
qa.a: Dilnaz kept one copy in the bag and one in a cloud folder.

qa.q: How does Dilnaz feel about the cancelled flight, judging by the letter?
qa.a: Dilnaz seems calm and quietly pleased that the earlier boring preparation turned the cancellation into a half-day delay.

qa.q: What steps let Dilnaz be booked on the evening flight?
qa.a: Dilnaz reached the airport early, joined the line before it was crowded and showed papers kept in two places.

qa.q: What might Pooja be thinking on reading about the checklist?
qa.a: Pooja is probably curious and relieved, wanting to copy the checklist and feel just as prepared on future trips.

grounding: Shows a prepared traveller keeping documents and contacts in two places, arriving early and having a plan when a flight is cancelled.

passage: You asked why I'm so fussy about travel. I'm Irfan, and I'll tell you about Lokesh's wedding in Jaipur. Two days before, I saved my tickets on my phone and emailed them to myself, kept a paper copy of my ID in my bag, and wrote three phone numbers in a notebook: Lokesh, his brother and the hotel. I reached the airport two hours early. At security, my phone died. No ticket, no contacts. I just handed over the paper copy and my ID. Then the flight was cancelled. I checked the next train on the station board and called the hotel from a borrowed phone, using my notebook. I reached the wedding four hours late, calm, instead of never.

qa.q: How early did Irfan reach the airport?
qa.a: Two hours early.

qa.q: How did Irfan feel when the phone died and the flight was cancelled?
qa.a: Irfan stayed calm, since the backups meant the problems were only inconveniences.

qa.q: Which of Irfan's preparations helped most?
qa.a: Keeping tickets and ID copies in two places, writing important numbers on paper and arriving early, which let Irfan switch plans quickly.

qa.q: How might Lokesh feel when Irfan arrived four hours late?
qa.a: Lokesh would likely feel relieved and happy that Irfan made it despite the cancelled flight.

grounding: A young adult describes keeping tickets, ID copies and contacts in two places and having a backup plan, turning disruption into inconvenience.

passage: I work at the same desk as Ujjwal, and I've always teased him about his travel folder. Before every work trip, he prints his tickets, keeps a photocopy of his ID, and writes the hotel address and three phone numbers on a card. Last month we flew to Kolkata together for a client meeting. At the airport, Mahima, our manager, found her phone had been stolen. No boarding pass, no contacts. She looked panicked. Ujjwal calmly pulled out his folder: he had the booking reference for all three of us and the hotel's number. The airline reprinted her pass. I can't say what Ujjwal felt, but he looked completely steady. I've started my own folder.

qa.q: What did Ujjwal write on his card?
qa.a: The hotel address and three phone numbers.

qa.q: How did Ujjwal seem during the airport problem?
qa.a: He looked completely steady and calm, unbothered by the stolen phone.

qa.q: How did Ujjwal's preparation turn a crisis into an inconvenience?
qa.a: Keeping printed tickets, booking references and contacts in a folder meant the airline could reprint Mahima's pass quickly.

qa.q: How did Mahima feel when she found her phone had been stolen?
qa.a: Mahima looked panicked, losing her boarding pass and contacts at once.

grounding: An observer describes a colleague whose paper backups of tickets and contacts turn a stolen phone into a small inconvenience.

passage:
Thursday. Wasim, twenty-five, had a job interview in Chennai on Monday. He booked the train for Sunday morning, not night, "in case anything goes wrong." He scanned his certificates and ID, emailed them to himself and kept printouts in a separate bag. He saved his friend Deepak's address in Chennai as a backup place to stay.
Sunday. The train was cancelled due to track repairs. Wasim felt his stomach drop, then remembered his plan. He took the afternoon bus instead.
Monday. He arrived at Deepak's flat at midnight, slept a few hours, and reached the interview office thirty minutes early, certificates in hand. The interviewer said, "Good, you're on time."

qa.q: Why was the train cancelled?
qa.a: Due to track repairs.

qa.q: How did Wasim feel when the train was cancelled?
qa.a: He felt his stomach drop with worry, then calmer as he remembered his backup plan.

qa.q: Which parts of Wasim's preparation saved the interview?
qa.a: Travelling a day early, keeping documents in two places and having Deepak's flat as a backup place to stay.

qa.q: How might Deepak feel when Wasim arrives at midnight?
qa.a: Deepak might be sleepy but glad to help, since the backup plan was agreed in advance.

grounding: Shows over several days a young adult whose backups and early travel turn a cancelled train into an inconvenience.

passage: "Sharmila, you're off on your first work trip, so let your Swati aunty tell you about mine. I was twenty-five, going to a training in Guwahati. My father made me do dull things the night before: two photocopies of my ID, one in the suitcase, one in my shoe bag; the ticket printed and also emailed to myself; my manager's number and the hotel's number on paper, not only in the phone. And he said, reach two hours early and know which train to take if the flight goes. Well. Fog. Flight cancelled. People were shouting at the counter. I went straight to the station, because I had the night train written down. Then at the station someone lifted my wallet. Real ID gone. The copy in my shoe bag got me on that train, and the paper numbers let me call the hotel. I arrived tired, not stranded. That's all preparation does, beta. It makes the bad day smaller."

qa.q: Where was young Swati's second ID photocopy?
qa.a: In her shoe bag.

qa.q: How might young Swati have felt when her wallet was stolen at the station?
qa.a: She was probably shocked and scared for a moment, then relieved to remember the copy in her shoe bag.

qa.q: Which of young Swati's preparations turned out to matter most, and why?
qa.a: The spare ID copy and the numbers on paper, because once the wallet was gone they were what got her on the train and in touch with the hotel.

qa.q: How might the people shouting at the counter have experienced the cancellation differently?
qa.a: Without a backup plan, they were stuck and angry, while Swati already knew her next step and went straight to the station.

grounding: Illustrates a traveller who keeps documents and contacts in two places, arrives early and has a backup route, so a cancellation and a theft become only an inconvenience.
